title: Frame Selection fails when ancestor CanvasItem is scaled
body:
### Tested versions

4.8-dev7
4.7.1 stable

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev7 - macOS Tahoe (26.4.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor (3360x2100 @ 60.00 Hz) - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads) - 8.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The `View menu -> Frame Selection` command (`Shift-F`) zooms to the wrong amount if the selected element has a `CanvasItem` ancestor with a non-`Vector2.ONE` scale.

For example, `CanvasItem.scale = Vector2(2.0, 2.0)` causes the zoom to be too close by a factor of 2.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82c9460c-f91a-4e0e-85f6-4f5e240398bf

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a 2D scene like this
```
Node2D
   `> CanvasItem      # set Scale to Vector2(2.0, 2.0)
       `> Sprite2D    # set texture to Godot icon
```

2. Use your mouse to zoom way out in the 2D Editor.
3. Select the `Sprite2D` in the Inspector.
4. Click `View -> Frame Selection`

**Expected results:** 

 - Godot icon takes up the full 2D Editor window.

**Actual results:** 
 - Godot icon is double-zoomed so you'd have to zoom out to see all of it.

Similar errors for `Vector2(0.1, 0.1)` (way zoomed out) or `Vector2(1.0, 2.0)` (width just fits, but too tall)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33078134/demo.zip)

Open `main.tscn` and follow the repro instructions above starting at step 2.
